I wrote /root/stage/beauty/guide_additions.md. It adds new sections 9 to 17 to BUILDING_GUIDE.md, plus helper pseudo-code and a sources list. I only read the code; I changed nothing in the generator or the Java.

**Why POIs spawn too high (ryan's actual question).** `StructureSiteRules.java` sets the whole build's height from the ground at its centre point only. The LAND score measures `dryMin`/`dryMax` but never uses them, so slope is not counted. On a rise, every lower edge floats, and `beard_thin` leaves the dirt wall seen in his screenshot.
- **Java fixes:**
  - Penalise slope: add `(dryMax - dryMin - 4) * 3` to the score when positive.
  - Set y 0 from the 30th percentile of the 25 sampled ground heights, so builds sink slightly rather than float.
  - Reject sites that would float more than about 6 blocks, except ESSENTIAL builds.
  - Use `beard_box` for forts.
- **Generator fixes:**
  - Deepen the `soften_edges` skirt (`skirt=12`, `reach=14`).
  - Run a foundation down to y -8 under every wall.
  - Add noise relief inside each site, with terraces and kinked retaining walls.
  - Make gardens and paths follow the local ground height (`ground_y`) instead of y 0.

**Shape:**
- Houses use L, T or offset plans with wings one floor lower.
- Neighbouring houses differ in height, and each group of 6 to 10 has one accent at least 1.6 times taller.
- Each house gets two or more add-ons: a bay window, porch, stair tower or balcony.

**Roofs:** at least two planes meeting at an angle on every house: cross-gables with valleys, dormers every 5 to 6 blocks, hip, saltbox or mansard, and flared curves on roofs 9 or more wide.

**Wall recipes per style:** timber frame with braces, stone, desert, Japanese and Venetian. The desert recipe includes a `desert_house()` with domes, projecting beam ends, varied parapets, striped awnings, arcades and roof items.

**Ground and towns:**
- Nothing organic runs more than 7 blocks straight.
- Paths wobble and have mixed edges; trees are branched and planted in groups of 3 to 5.
- Towns grow from bending streets, with odd-shaped plazas and plots of different sizes.

**Ships:** all sails belly the same way, and ships at a dock have their sails furled. Rigging always runs between two solid blocks.

The audit checklist has 12 measurable checks, including no wall run over 5 blocks and a site outline under 92% of its bounding box.

The base is built into the cliffs, and the famous dock is a huge cavern inside the rock that ships enter through a giant sea gate. Here it is a flat lawn plate, the 'harbour' is a round pit open to the sky, and the sea gate is a slot at the very edge of the canvas.

The report says 'edge columns left out=0' because andesite/cobblestone/tuff in the rock stack make soften_edges skip every column, so in the world this sits as a square stone block. Ryugu Palace in the anime is a tall, organic coral and shell castle: pink and white with many spiral-shell spires, a large central dome and its own bubble. It sits on a hill above the town, and the island has the giant Eve tree whose roots bring sunlight. Here the palace is a small, low, square pink block with four round turrets and a few shell spires, and the white tiers look like a wedding cake. The fish-man town shell houses are hidden in a few tiny clusters.
The island floor is mostly an empty white-sand ring between the outer glass and the palace pit. Very few houses are spread round it.

Make the palace big and vertical: a cluster of tapering spiral-shell spires of varied height, a large central pearl dome, coral arches and balconies, in pink, white and pearl, filling its own bubble.
Add the Eve tree: huge roots arching over the island from the ocean floor into the bubble, with sunlight shafts (glowstone or froglight beams).
Fill the bubble floor with the Fish-Man District: dense shell houses, coral streets, Mermaid Cove, kelp gardens and bubble lamps on posts, with level changes.
Give the glass bubble a smoother shell (fewer stepped bands) or mixed glass tints so it reads as a bubble, and make the inside visible from the cutaways.

Make the lighthouse a tapered tower with a gallery, arched windows and a lantern room, and use layered palm crowns (drooping fronds) for the palms.

problems.code_hint: g5_base.py: b.walls(... light_gray_concrete), b.box(... 21 ...) flat roof, text on a plain concrete board

problems.where: fortress wall and the five watchtowers
problems.detail: The walls are 9-high sheer gray_concrete with a single blue line. The towers are hollow 7x7 concrete boxes. There are no buttresses, no gate arch, no walkway and no texture: concrete everywhere, against the guide.
Polished andesite with snow layers sprinkled at random reads as TV static over the whole yard: no paths, no drill lines, no shovelled lanes.
B.ship draws flat split sails with no yard. The ship is a brown pirate-style hull, not a Marine warship (no white hull, no gull figurehead, no MARINE sails).
problems.code_hint: B.ship in tools/worldgen/kit.py flat sail plane

problems.where: Marine flag on the HQ roof
problems.detail: The flag is a flat 8x5 wool plate on a concrete pole.
Marine bases in the show are white with blue trim and roofs, MARINE lettering and the gull emblem, and G-5 is famously rowdy and messy. This is a black-and-grey prison box with no Marine identity.

top_fixes: Rebuild the HQ in white marine_bricks with blue tile roofs and a central tower; step the facade, add pilasters and paint a big readable G-5 and gull on a white panel
Give the walls texture (marine bricks with variants), buttresses every 8 blocks, a walkway with railing and a proper arched sea gate; make the towers round or octagonal with roofs
Make the yard look used: shovelled snow lanes, piles of snow against the walls, crates, a beer-barrel mess (G-5 is rowdy), drill lines
Replace the B.ship call with a proper Marine battleship (white hull, gull figurehead, billowing MARINE sails)
Use a 2-thick waving flag with the gull instead of a flat plate

problems.detail: A dark mud grid covers the entire ground: straight lines every 7 blocks in both directions, like graph paper. It comes from `(x*z) % 7 == 0`, which is true on every column where x or z is a multiple of 7. This is the most obvious flaw in the build.
problems.code_hint: straw_shrine.py build(): `"minecraft:mud" if (x * z) % 7 == 0 else grass_block`

problems.where: hanging straw dolls on the dead trees
problems.detail: The finish report says 'removed floating bit=139' and 'propped up floating part=10'. The fence 'rope' starts at h-3 but the branch tip is at h-1, so there is a one-block gap at h-2, and the finishing pass deletes most of the hanging dolls. What's left are bare dead trees.
problems.code_hint: straw_shrine.py tree loop: branch at y=h-2-k+j//2 (j=3 -> h-1), fences at h-2-j for j in 1,2 -> h-3,h-4

problems.detail: The Straw Man is a yellow blob with two straight horizontal arms (a T-pose of hay cylinders) and a pixel face. Hawkins' straw form is a tall, thin, menacing straw figure with long spiky arms, nails driven in and straw tufts. This one reads as a hay-block snowman.
The crew tents are solid white wool wedges, one block thick per row.

The torii are red concrete with a black concrete lintel, flat colour with no curved kasagi. The shrine hall is a gloom-plank box with a pagoda roof but no engawa, steps or offering box. Hawkins' look (tarot, straw, a misty, eerie swamp) needs fog, lanterns and hanging dolls.
The platform is a flat 33x33 stone-brick square with a sparse wall-post rim.

top_fixes: Replace the `(x*z)%7` mud with noise-based patches, and add swamp texture (mud, moss carpets, roots, reeds, puddles)
Fix the hanging-doll rope so it starts directly under the branch tip (fence or chain from h-2 down), so the dolls survive the finishing pass
Re-sculpt the Straw Man: taller and thinner, with long angled spiky arms, straw tufts sticking out, iron-nail details and a hunched pose
Give the torii a curved kasagi and use vermilion wood or terracotta in place of concrete; add stone lanterns along the boardwalk
Break up the platform: steps, a raised hall base with engawa, an offering box, a gravel garden
Make proper tents (pole frame, sloped canvas with depth, open flaps)

problems.detail: The pit is seven perfectly circular concentric terraces with a dotted ring of bars, which reads as a dartboard. A mine pit should be irregular, with ramps, wooden scaffolding, cranes, carts and spoil heaps.

The surface is a flat brown plate of coarse dirt with dead bushes. Under it is a solid square block of stone and deepslate down to y -36, with sheer sides. The report says 'edge columns left out=0' because deepslate in the stack stops soften_edges from touching it, so in the world this sits as a giant square cube. This matches ryan's 'spawns higher than it should / not natural'.
problems.code_hint: udon_prison.py fills deepslate/stone from -DEPTH-8 to -3 under all 96x96; pipeline.soften_edges bare() rejects deepslate

problems.detail: In the anime Udon is a huge walled prison: tall stone and timber walls, the Beasts Pirates' jolly-roger banners, big wooden gates, watchtowers, prisoners hauling rock in a quarry under guards, Queen's headliner office, and the oshiruko (red-bean soup) mess. Here the palisade is a ring of short log posts, the 'gate' is two thin dark boxes with tiny roofs and no gate between them, the soup cauldron is a tiny iron ring, and there are no Beasts Pirates symbols.
The cells are 1-wide, 3-deep notches with a carpet or cobweb inside. Cut -9 shows them as a fringe of holes, not cell rows with doors and walkways.
The purple frame over the ring is a thin wool line on four bare posts, with no roof. A sumo ring (dohyo) would have a hanging roof, tassels and a raised clay ring.

problems.where: the two storage huts and the watch office
problems.detail: The storage huts are plain plank boxes with slab roofs. The watch office interior is the only furnished part.

top_fixes: Make the pit irregular: noise-varied terrace radii, switchback ramps, wooden scaffolds and ladders on the walls, cranes, mine carts on rails and spoil heaps
Build the prison wall: tall stone-base, timber-top walls with walkways, Beasts Pirates banners, a big double gate between the towers, and watchtowers with roofs
Make cell rows as recessed galleries with bars, doors and a railed walkway in front
Give the sumo ring a proper dohyo: raised clay ring, a hanging roof with purple tassels, and seating
Remove the square deepslate block or let soften_edges work (only stone/dirt in the outer columns) so it doesn't sit as a cube in the world
Add the oshiruko mess hall with a giant cauldron and long tables

problems.detail: The houses are identical plain sandstone boxes with crenellated tops and a coloured awning. This is the exact Nanohana look ryan hates. Alabasta houses in the show are rounded adobe with domes, arched doors, rooftop terraces and cloth shades.
problems.code_hint: yuba_oasis.py: AL.house(...) from alubarna.py for every house

problems.detail: The dunes are whole-block stair terraces with hard contour edges (int(dune())), a few random slabs and no ripples. They don't bury the houses to their roofs as the docstring says. The houses stand clear on the steps.
The dead palms are single 1-wide palm-log posts 4-8 high with no crown, scattered like fence posts. They read as stray sticks.

Yuba in the show was a large oasis town swallowed by sandstorms: half-buried big buildings, Toto's lone dig pit with his shovel, and the inn where the crew slept. Here the 'dry lake' is a small shallow oval and the tents are solid wool wedges. There is no sense of a dying big town and nothing recognisable apart from the pit.

problems.where: Toto's tent and the rebel tents
problems.detail: The tents are solid wool triangles with no poles, flaps or rope lines.
The house interiors are small square rooms of random clutter, with sand drifting into none of them.

top_fixes: Replace AL.house with varied adobe buildings: rounded corners, domes, arched doorways, rooftop terraces and cloth canopies, with some partly collapsed
Make the dunes smooth with slabs/layers and wind ripples, and actually pour sand over houses (into windows, up to rooftops), with some buildings showing only a dome
Give dead palms bent trunks with drooping dead fronds (or snapped tops) instead of straight posts
Widen and deepen the dry lake bed with cracked mud and an old stone rim; make Toto's pit the focal point with a shovel, buckets and a rope ladder
Build proper tents with pole frames and sloped canvas, and a ruined inn for the crew

problems.detail: The whole build is one dead-flat square lawn (moss and grass at y0) with an oval pond. It is meant to be an archipelago of jungle islets, but there are no islands, no channels, no hills and no undergrowth layers.

The third giant vine runs from (96,1,30) to (64,22,8) and ends 22 blocks up in mid-air. Its free end hangs over nothing, and the finish pass reports 'propped up floating part=3, removed floating bit=8'.
problems.where: NE corner, x~64 z~8 y~22 (brown segment top-right in cut22)

problems.detail: The 'greenhouse' is a plain pale-blue glass box with a flat glass lid. The snapper plants are a concrete post with two red slabs. The pitcher plants are smooth lime-concrete tubes. Everything is flat concrete, with no gradients and no texture.
Heracles' treehouse is one plank box on a pole with a hip roof. Inside are two small furnish() zones, reached only by a 12-block ladder. It has no specimen jars, no bug cages and no balcony.

Boin Archipelago in the anime is a dense, wildly colourful jungle of absurdly oversized plants: carnivorous flowers, giant fruit, bulbous mushrooms, a canopy that blocks the sky, and Heracles' hut among the roots. Here, about a dozen props stand far apart on an open field. The sunflower face is a single block thick and reads as a flat disc.

top_fixes: Rebuild the terrain as 3-5 jungle islets of different heights separated by muddy channels and mangrove roots, with undulating ground, giant ferns, moss mounds and dense layered undergrowth. Fill the space instead of leaving open lawn.
Make every vine end in the ground or wrap around a plant: fix the third vine so it lands at y1, and add hanging tendrils and leaves along the vines.

Rebuild the plants with texture and gradients: pitcher plants of lime/green terracotta and moss with a ribbed, flared lip and a lid; snappers with jaws and teeth made of stairs; a sunflower 2-3 thick with layered petals and a seed-pattern face. Add giant fruit and carnivorous flowers.

Turn Heracles' lab into a cozy workshop in the roots: jars (glass with candles inside), bug nets, cages, shelves and planters, a spiral stair around the trunk and a railed balcony. Give the greenhouse a framed, pitched glass roof with posts.
Add a canopy layer of giant leaves overhead, so that from above the island reads as jungle and not as a lawn.

problems.detail: The HQ is four plain smooth-sandstone boxes stacked as a ziggurat. Each tier is a flat wall with a slit window every 3 blocks and one band of crenels. No buttresses, set-backs, pilasters, arcades, balconies or roof detail. This is the Nanohana look ryan hates.
problems.code_hint: build(): tiers loop with b.walls/b.box; windows `for x in range(..., 3)` black panes only

problems.detail: The curtain wall is a single 9-high flat cut-sandstone slab with an even crenel row. It has no buttresses, wall walk, machicolations, gatehouse or material change. The gate is just a 7-wide hole (CX-3..CX+3) that you can't even see in the renders.

problems.where: 8 outer houses in two straight columns at x=10 and x=84
problems.detail: These are identical sand-style townkit houses with flat roofs in a grid, the same barracks box repeated.

The ground is a dead-flat sand plate with white concrete powder on a regular (x*5+z*3)%11 dot grid, which reads as a polka-dot pattern. The pink training posts stand in a ruler-straight row. There are no dunes inside, no rock outcrops, no paving or plazas.
The 'dragon-wing banners' are 1-wide black wool columns with a red dot. In the renders they read as black posts stuck to the wall, not banners.
problems.code_hint: for x in range(WX0+6, WX1-4, 14): black_wool column at WZ1+1

problems.detail: The outside stairs between terraces and the tower ladders are both disabled with `if False`, so the only way up is a single ladder column. The terraces have no stairs and no railings.
problems.code_hint: stairs(...) if False else None; ladder ... if False else None

problems.detail: In the anime Baltigo is a bone-white island of white sand and pale rock, and the HQ is a tall, jagged white stone fortress on a rocky rise. Here it is warm tan sandstone on yellow sand. The palette is wrong, and there are no rocky crags and no large Revolutionary Army flags.
The rooms are subdivide grids of generic barracks and library. Dragon's 'world map' is random blue and lime concrete noise. The cut at y=20 shows a dark empty grid floor in the top tier.

top_fixes: Rebuild the palette as bone-white: calcite, diorite, bone block, white terracotta and pale sand, with darker stone at the base. Add rocky white crags and dune ridges inside the walls.

Replace the box ziggurat with a fortress that has set-backs, buttresses every 6-8 blocks, arcaded terraces, balconies, a tall central tower with a proper cap and big black Revolutionary flags (2-thick, double-sided).
Give the curtain wall buttresses, a wall walk with a parapet, and a real gatehouse with an arched gate and flanking towers. Vary its height and follow the terrain.
Break the house grid: different sizes and heights, domes and arches, arrange them along winding lanes, and add awnings and market stalls.
Re-enable the terrace stairs with railings, and paint a readable world map (blue sea with land shapes) in Dragon's room.

problems.where: all shacks (4 rows on a 9-block grid)
problems.detail: About 30 shacks are identical 6-8 block boxes in four straight rows on a 9-block pitch. From above the town is a checkerboard of lumps.
problems.code_hint: for z0 in (30,44,18,54): for x0 in range(4, NX-9, 9): shack(...)

problems.detail: Each shack is a 4-high single-material box with 4 random patch blocks. It has no posts or frame, and no lean-to, porch or awning.
The 'slumped straw roof' is a flat 1-2 high hay/slab checker, (x*3+z*7)%4. It reads as noisy yellow-brown cubes, not a sagging thatch or board roof, and has no overhang shape or slope.
The washing is carpets placed at y=3 between fence posts. Carpets in the air get deleted by finish ('removed floating carpet' x15), so the laundry lines are gone entirely.
The ground is flat coarse dirt with a regular (x*7+z*3)%6 mud dot pattern. The grave mound (sphere at y=-1, ry=3) barely shows. The river is a straight band.

Ebisu Town in Wano is a crooked, sprawling slum of leaning timber huts with sagging plank and straw roofs, patched cloth, smoke, junk piles and smiling townsfolk, along a polluted dark river. The shrine here is a red concrete cube, and the Toko dango stall and soup kitchen are generic stalls.

top_fixes: Lay the shacks along winding lanes at random angles and sizes, cluster some into lean-to rows, and add porches, awnings, stilts and junk piles.
Build real sagging roofs: stair/slab gables or lean-to slopes of spruce and dark oak with straw patches and a dip in the middle, overhanging by 1.
Give the walls a spruce-log frame with mixed plank infill, cloth patches (wool or banners), paper windows and broken boards.
Hang the laundry on chains or a string line attached at both ends: banners or wool on a fence rail, not floating carpets.
Raise a real grave mound with stones and incense, add a small Wano shrine with a torii and roof, and make the river murky with mud banks and junk.

problems.detail: The warehouse is one 44x26x14 blue concrete box with steel posts every 4 blocks. Its 'sawtooth' roof rises only 2 blocks per tooth, so it reads as flat grey stripes. It has no salvage character: no mismatched plates, rust, pipes or add-ons.

problems.where: north and back faces of the signs (NW view)
problems.detail: The FRANKY board and the star backing are single-thick blue concrete slabs. From the back they are huge blank blue walls standing on the roof, with the text written on one side only.
problems.code_hint: blue_concrete box at Z1 for the lettering; fill_if star backing

problems.detail: scrap_heap() scatters random blocks at random points in each layer, so the upper layers are disconnected confetti. 36 bits were removed as floating. What remains is multicoloured noise (anvils, coal, copper) with gaps, not a pile.
The ground floor is a huge empty grey andesite floor with a few blocks. The 'Battle Franky robots' are two stacked iron/blue boxes. The upper gallery is a strip of generic subdivide rooms.

In Water 7 Franky House is a ramshackle hideout on the scrapyard shore: a big rough building topped by a huge 'FRANKY HOUSE' sign, surrounded by mountains of junk and Franky Family bikes, with the Square Sisters' boats at a quay. A tidy blue concrete factory with a cola bar does not read as Franky's.
The Square Sisters' boats are two flat coloured slabs floating on the water.

top_fixes: Rebuild the house as a patched salvage building: mixed iron, copper and plank plates, an asymmetric roofline, exterior pipes, ladders, a balcony, and a crooked lean-to garage.
Make the sign a proper 2-thick billboard reading 'FRANKY HOUSE' on both sides, with a steel lattice support, plus Franky's star.
Rewrite scrap_heap as solid mounds (filled sphere or heightfield) with rusty blocks on the surface, and stick out beams, wheels and chains that touch the pile.
Fill the garage with half-built machines on stands, a workbench wall, chains with hooks from beams, and cola barrels; give the party hall a bar and a stage.
Build real Yagara-bull boats and the Square Sisters' boat with hulls, and add cranes over the quay with chains reaching down to cargo.

problems.detail: The inside of the build is a dead-flat sand plate, speckled at random with coarse dirt (15%) and dead bushes. There are no dunes, no rubble mounds and no street level changes. It reads as a sheet of paper with a hole in it.
problems.code_hint: build(): T.ground(...) plus the 'rnd.random()<0.15 coarse_dirt' loop

problems.detail: 12 identical T.house 'sand' boxes, 11x9 with flat roofs, sit in a ring at fixed grid positions. They have no domes, arches, arcades or stair-towers, so it is not the Arabian desert town the show has.
problems.code_hint: for i,(x,z) in enumerate(hs): T.house(..., flat_roof=True)

problems.detail: The fire damage is per-block random noise that turns blocks into AIR or scattered blackstone, coal or basalt. Every house becomes swiss cheese with single-block holes and polka-dot black blocks, not believable ruins: no collapsed roof sections, fallen charred beams, rubble heaps at wall feet, or soot streaks rising from the windows.
problems.code_hint: the 'fire damage' loop over b.blocks (burn*0.55 -> AIR/BURNT)

problems.detail: The burn pass deletes blocks that held up carpets, flower boxes and lamps. The finish pass then had to delete 11 red carpets, 7 black carpets, 6 flower boxes and a wall lamp, and propped up a floating part. One loose sandstone block floats off the west rim.
problems.where: houses near the crater; a single block at about canvas (148,460) in the SE view
problems.code_hint: burn loop runs after T.house and does not respect what is attached

problems.detail: The crater is a perfect round bowl, a paraboloid of depth 8, with a random checker of blackstone, magma and tinted glass. It has no raised blast rim, no radial scorch rays, no half-swallowed buildings sliding in, and no glassy melted streaks.

The 'ruined clock tower' is a solid sandstone wedge with a quartz plus-sign for a clock. Banaro's skyline in the show is domed adobe houses and a tall tower. Blackbeard's camp is just a stone tavern with a dark gable roof that does not fit the desert style.
problems.code_hint: ruined clock tower block; T.house(... style='stone', kinds=('tavern',))

problems.detail: The house interiors are standard furnish rooms scorched to coal. There is no sense of a battle aftermath: no overturned tables, broken barrels, ash or fire still burning.

top_fixes: Replace T.house(flat_roof) with real Alabasta-style adobe: varied heights (1-3 floors), small domes, arched doorways and windows, outside stairs up to roof terraces, timber beam ends (vigas) sticking out of the walls, and mixed sandstone, terracotta and smooth sandstone.

Make the ruins structured, not noise: knock out whole roof sections and upper wall corners in chunks facing the crater, then pile rubble (stairs/slabs/cobble) at the wall feet, add charred dark-oak beams leaning out of the gaps and soot (blackstone/basalt) streaks above the windows.
Give the crater a raised, broken rim, scorched rays fanning out on the ground, and half-swallowed houses tilting into the pit. Keep it irregular (noise on the radius and depth).
Shape the ground with low dunes and street level changes. Add rubble mounds and drifts of sand against the walls instead of a speckled flat plate.
Rebuild the clock tower as a real tower (square shaft, clock face with a frame, broken belfry top) and give Blackbeard's tavern a desert style with the Jolly Roger on a proper two-sided flag.
Run the burn pass before furnishing, or skip blocks that hold attachables, so carpets and flower boxes are not left floating.

problems.where: the whole cavern, a forest of grey-blue vertical lines between the cell blocks and the cauldron (cut 9 and cut 16)
problems.detail: The finish pass placed 2140 lights, each a chandelier hung 4 above the floor on an iron chain up to 30 blocks long from the cave roof. The open floor reads as hundreds of dangling chains, which is ugly and unnatural.
problems.code_hint: finish.place_light(): `if h >= 6: ly = y + 4; for k in range(ly+1, y+h): iron_chain` with h allowed up to 30

problems.where: lift shaft at the north (LX=50, LZ=6), sticking out above the rock dome in both exterior views
problems.detail: The seastone lift shaft is built to H+6 and pokes through the cavern shell as a teal column standing in the open. It looks as if the structure spawned too high or the shell is missing.
problems.code_hint: `b.box(LX-3, 0, LZ-3, LX+3, H+6, LZ+3, seastone_bricks)` while the shell ends at H+thick

problems.detail: A flat blackstone disc with random magma dots. No rock outcrops, no stepped levels, no rubble, no stalagmites or lava channels. The cauldron is a plain nether-brick ring.

In the anime, Level 4 is a huge furnace hall dominated by the giant Boiling Blood Cauldron. A narrow iron bridge hangs over it, with prisoners hauling firewood and roaring furnace fires everywhere, under a red-orange glow. Here the bridge is a flat white slab (iron trapdoors) and there are no stacks of firewood, no furnace mouths in the walls and no orange heat haze. The cells are dark stacked boxes.
Plain seastone and blackstone boxes with flat roofs and a few panes stand free on the cave floor.
problems.code_hint: b.walls(OX0, 1, OZ0, OX1, 11, OZ1, seastone_bricks); I.subdivide(...)

problems.where: chained posts scattered on the floor
problems.detail: A dark-oak post 3 tall with a single chain block on top holds nothing.

top_fixes: For caves, cap hung lights at about 8 blocks of chain. Light the floor with braziers, fire grates, shroomlight or magma seams set into the cave roof and walls, and lava channels in the floor instead of chandeliers on 30-block chains (fix in finish.place_light for mode 'cave', or give underground builds their own lights).
Stop the lift shaft at the shell (H+thick) or bury it in a rock column that carries on up, so nothing teal sticks out of the dome.

Make the cauldron the hero: a huge raised iron and nether-brick pot 6-8 tall with a rim, bubbling lava, glowing rim and steam (campfires), and a narrow rope-and-iron bridge sagging in a catenary on chains anchored into the roof.
Add furnace mouths of blackstone with fire in the cavern walls, woodpiles and log stacks, minecart tracks, uneven floor levels, rock pillars and stalactites.
Give the office and barracks real facades: pilasters, a cornice, barred windows with frames, and a roof that meets the cave rock.

problems.where: the four corners of the two cell rows (x 16..87 at z 20 and z 69), poking out of the obsidian shell at the corners in both exterior views
problems.detail: The cell rows are 10 cells x 7 = 71 long. At z offset 28 from the centre the ellipse is only about 62 wide, so the end cells of both tiers cut through the cave shell and stick out into open space as teal boxes. The shell is broken, and in-game the cells would open into the surrounding rock and lava.

problems.where: the sealed shaft (CX, z 4..10), sticking out above the dome
problems.detail: Built to H+4, the seastone shaft stands above the cavern shell as a free teal column.

problems.where: the open hall between the cell rows (cut 9 and cut 15)
problems.detail: Dozens of long dark chains with chandeliers hang from the cave ceiling, plus 40 parts the finish pass had to hang from the ceiling. The chains inside the cells were 2 blocks at y+3..y+4 with a gap below the ceiling.
problems.code_hint: finish.place_light (h up to 30); the cell-chain loop `b.set(x, y + 4, cz, iron_chain); b.set(x, y + 3, ...)`

problems.detail: A flat deepslate plate with a regular (x+z)%6 diagonal stripe of tiles and straight rows of soul-fire markers. Featureless and gridded.

Level 6 has no treasure vault. In the anime it is a dim, oppressive corridor of huge sealed cells where the worst prisoners (Ace before his transfer, Crocodile, Jinbe, Shiliew's era) sit chained to walls in seastone shackles. It needs heavy cell doors, wall shackles and a tight, heavy atmosphere. A big vault with gold blocks in the middle breaks the theme.
Identical teal boxes in two straight rows with bars across the front. No wall shackles, no worn prisoner benches, no grime or variation.

top_fixes: Size the cell rows to the cave (shorter rows, or curve them along the ellipse), or carve the cave wider, so no cell breaks the shell. Then check that no shell column is missing.
Cut the shaft off at the shell, or wrap it in rock up to the canvas top, so nothing protrudes.
Light with soul-fire braziers in wall niches and soul lanterns on short chains under a lower vaulted ceiling with ribs, not chandeliers on 25-block chains.
Swap the central vault for a chained-prisoner cell block or the execution/transfer room. Add wall shackles (chains into the wall), seastone doors, puddles and cracked deepslate.
Break the floor with drainage channels, raised walkways, rubble and noise-based tile variants instead of a modulo stripe.

problems.where: the Red Line itself, the whole cliff block
problems.detail: The Red Line is a perfect rectangular cuboid 40 tall with ruler-straight horizontal colour bands every 5 blocks. Two faces have a few ledges, but the north and west faces are completely flat striped walls. It looks like a cake slice, or like the structure spawned 40 blocks too high on flat ground.
problems.code_hint: mary_geoise.build(): `RED if (y // 5) % 3 else orange/terracotta` per y over a rectangular footprint

problems.where: the top of the Red Line
problems.detail: A bare quartz and white-concrete 4x4 checkerboard plaza over the whole summit, with a few tiny fountains and statues. No gardens, trees, paths or level changes. The guide says never checkerboard.

A plain white box with flat roofs and a stepped dome sunk into the roof. The four corner towers are plain round shafts with blobby yellow 'onion' caps that look like cauliflowers. The mansions are white boxes with stepped pyramid roofs.

In the anime, Pangaea Castle is a towering white palace with many tall spires and a high central tower (the Empty Throne and the flower room). It is surrounded by lush green parkland, rivers, bridges and the opulent mansions of the Celestial Dragons. The Bondola lift climbs a rugged, crimson cliff with a misty face, from Red Port below. The port at the bottom is just an orange plate with four flat dark boxes.

problems.where: Red Port at the foot of the cliff
problems.detail: Flat orange plate with four identical low boxes with dark flat roofs. No docks, water, ships or Bondola station.
Mostly rectangular rooms with carpet. The Empty Throne hall does not read as a grand space with the throne and the swords of the 20 kings.

top_fixes: Make the Red Line a real cliff: noise-carved face with overhangs, crags, vertical fissures, mixed red terracotta, red sandstone and granite in irregular strata, ledges with dead bushes, and a less square footprint. Stop it reading as a 40-high box spawned on flat ground.
Replace the checker plaza with parkland: lawns, trees, flower beds, canals or streams with arched bridges, gravel paths and terraced levels.

Rebuild Pangaea Castle as a vertical spired palace: tall central tower, many slender spires with gold conical caps, flying buttresses, colonnades and a grand stair. Make the gold domes smooth ribbed onions rather than blobs.
Turn Red Port into a harbour with water, piers, ships, a Bondola station and warehouses.
Give the Empty Throne hall a raised throne with the 20 swords round it, columns and a vaulted ceiling.

problems.where: the whole open cavern (cut 8 and cut 14)
problems.detail: Dozens of long thin chains with lights hang from the 26-high cave ceiling all over the garden and between the halls. It reads like rain or a cage, not a party. Three froglights were placed in mid-air at H-6 and removed as floating.
problems.code_hint: finish.place_light (long chains); `b.set(x, H - 6 - abs(x - CX)//4, z, pearlescent_froglight)`

problems.where: party hall, bar and kitchen block, bedroom block, throne room
problems.detail: Every building is a flat-roofed terracotta box from hall() or I.subdivide, with a gold block every other block on the top course and a row of pink glass. Muted maroon, magenta and purple boxes with nothing gaudy about them.
A flat crimson nylium plate with random tufts and a few nether-wart-blob trees. The disco floor is a strict checkerboard of concrete and shroomlight.

Newkama Land in the anime is a loud, neon okama paradise: a giant stage with Ivankov's huge face on it, bright spotlights, banners, a big bar, hot springs and colourful flashy decor everywhere. This build is dim, maroon and boxy, without the 'Newkama Kenpo' energy, an Ivankov emblem, light shows or giant props.
Standard furnish() rooms with nothing Newkama-specific: no costumes on stands, mirrors, makeup tables or flamboyant decor.

top_fixes: Use a lighting style for this cave with no long ceiling chains: glowing crystal and froglight clusters attached to the roof, neon strips (coloured glass over light) along buildings, and floor spotlights.

Build a huge stage with a giant Ivankov head or face and his crown as the backdrop, a proscenium arch, curtains on both sides, light rigs anchored to the roof, and a proper dance floor pattern (radial or striped, not a checker).
Make the buildings flamboyant: curved or onion roofs, striped awnings, marquee signs with text, heart-shaped windows, pink and gold pillars. Break the flat roofs and add balconies.
Vary the cave floor with levels, steps, a hot-spring pool with steam among rocks, and paths, rather than a flat nylium plate.
Furnish the dressing rooms with armor stands in costumes, mirrors (glass panes and frames), vanity tables and wardrobes.

problems.detail: The Sexy Foxy's two masts carry flat orange wool rectangles, made by kit.ship's flat sails. The hull is generic, with no fox-head figurehead.

The commentators' booth is a plank box at y11-14 behind the south grandstand. It rests on nothing except where it clips into the awning, and has no posts or stair. The bunting strings are single lanterns and lone wool blocks at y7/y8 with no string between them; the finish pass removed 3 floating lanterns and added 33 chains to prop things up.
problems.where: booth x42-46 z11-14 y11; bunting x8-74 z50 y7-8

problems.detail: Foxy's command tent is a box with vertical walls up to y5 that then steps in one block per layer, so it reads as a striped ziggurat or box, not a tent. There is no peak, no draped canvas, no guy ropes and no scalloped valance. The crew's tents are tiny solid wool prisms.
The pitch is a flat rectangle of striped grass and moss inside a flat field, with two plain stepped grandstands of acacia planks. Nothing grounds it in the landscape.

Long Ring Long Land's identity is missing: the long, thin ring-shaped island strips; Tonjit's house on its absurdly tall stilts; the stretched animals; the rolling grassland with tall, very slender trees with flat tops. The trees here are birch sticks with one leaf ball, lined up along one edge. The Groggy Ring has no crowd stands of Foxy Pirates with flags, and the Donut Race start is just a checkered strip.
Inside the tent there are only two furnish() rooms (tavern and throne) on a plank floor. There is no stage, no banners, no Foxy throne on a dais and no lighting rig.

top_fixes: Replace b.ship with b.hull + b.square_sail (billowing sails with a fox emblem) and add a big fox-head figurehead. Sit the ship at the end of a proper pier.
Put the commentators' booth on timber legs with a ladder, or attach it to the grandstand back with brackets. Run real bunting: chains or fences between poles with wool pennants hanging from them.
Make Foxy's tent a real big top: a centre pole, draped canvas that slopes out from the peak, a scalloped valance, guy ropes to stakes, a flag on top, and a striped entrance awning.

Shape the land like Long Ring Long Land: long narrow grassy strips with sea inlets between them, gentle swells, tall slender trees with flat leafy tops scattered through the land, and Tonjit's stilt house towering on a 30+ block pole.
Give the grandstands detail: posts, railings, Foxy flags, colour bands, a judge's box and stairs. Add the goal rings' supporting frames and a referee platform.

problems.detail: Chocolate Town is a grid of identical boxes: every sweet_house is a rectangle with a flat frosting-slab roof and a single red block or candle on top, placed at fixed spots in four corner clusters along a square street grid. This is exactly the 'boxes in a grid' ryan hates.

The Mirror Hall drum is 20 blocks of tinted glass between blackstone piers, which reads as a featureless black cylinder. The entrance hall is a plain black box. The pink stained-glass dome renders as opaque pink layers, so the hall looks like a black-and-pink cake.

The mochi tower starts at y24 (TOPY+4), inside the hollow glass dome, where there is no floor or roof slab under it. Its base hangs 13 blocks above the floor-2 deck. The 6 mochi 'arms' are sphere chains going out into the air.

In the anime, the Mirro-World is a reflected mirror dimension full of mirror panes and odd stretched spaces, and Cacao Island's Chocolate Town is a whimsical port of melting chocolate buildings with swirling roofs and cream. Neither reads here.
The ground is a flat square of grass with a straight mud-brick street grid and a disc of granite around the hall.
The throne is a quartz block with a stair and some wool blobs. The rooms are furnish() boxes with tinted-glass dividers. The 'donut feast' is a row of cakes.

top_fixes: Rebuild the houses as varied candy architecture: curved and melting chocolate walls with drips, swirl and cupcake roofs in different shapes and heights, cookie frames, candy-cane posts, wafer awnings. Lay them along winding streets instead of a grid.
Give the hall exterior relief: framed mirror panels with gold trim, buttresses, a grand entrance arch with a mirror portal, and a dome of clear or light glass on gold ribs instead of opaque pink.
Ground the mochi tower: start it from the hall floor (or a roof slab under the dome) and let it rise through an opening. Anchor the arms to the dome or have them drape down onto it.
Add mirror-world motifs: reflected and duplicated rooms, mirror corridors with panes on both sides, and an upside-down part.
Give Katakuri's throne room a real dais, a mochi-draped throne, the secret snack lounge (sofa, donut towers, tea) and shelves.

problems.detail: The 'great stepped temple' is four stacked solid boxes, each 3 blocks smaller, with a chiseled-tuff dot every 2 blocks and a cube shrine on top. There are no stairs on the other faces, no carvings, no colonnade and no doorway frame. Almost everything is grey tuff, so it reads as a lump.

The statue's 'broken crown' is a 15x5 slab at y10-11 set across the top of a 12-wide head sphere that comes to a point at y10. It rests on a single point, and the finish pass propped up a floating part. The fallen gate rubble steps between y1 and y2, so some pieces hang in the air.
problems.where: statue head x79-93 z28-32; gate rubble x53-64 z~95

problems.detail: A Void Century kingdom should feel colossal and mysterious: giant carved faces and hands, Poneglyph-style glyph walls, a huge collapsed statue (like Emet or the ancient giant robot), and overgrown ruins. Here the 'statue' is a sphere with two black dots and a box hand.
The hall of murals is stripes of glazed terracotta along two walls. The archive is a deepslate box with two furnish() zones and a 2-block poneglyph.
The plaza is one flat polished tuff disc of radius 30 with two chiseled rings. The roofless houses are rectangles of random-height walls.

top_fixes: Rebuild the temple as a real stepped pyramid: stairs on all faces, a carved colonnaded sanctum on top, glyph friezes, a sun disc. Mix in sandstone, gilded blackstone or verdigris copper accents so it is not all grey.

Sculpt a real toppled giant: a large carved face lying on its side with nose, brow and cracked crown resting on the ground, a separate open hand, and broken limbs half buried. Remove the floating crown slab.
Lay the rubble on the ground (all at y1, some half sunk), and add vines, moss and roots overgrowing the ruins.
Break up the plaza with cracked paving, broken stairs, a sunken court and terraces at different levels. Give the house ruins doorways, window gaps and fallen roof beams.
Make the archive feel sacred: a large Poneglyph cube on a dais, glyph walls, candles and a vaulted ceiling.

problems.where: all 12 cottages on Lovely Street (ring round the centre)
problems.detail: Every house is the same grey half-sphere with one blue band, ribs and a pole on top, set out evenly round an oval. They look like stone igloos or bunkers. White concrete renders flat grey with no texture.
problems.code_hint: cottage(): cyl + dome in white_concrete, light_blue_concrete band, the same for every house

problems.where: the island interior between the houses
problems.detail: The cloud island is one flat white plate at y 0 with a single-block white/blue path drawn on it. There are no cloud mounds, puffy hills, dunes or soft terraces; only the outer rim gets puffs.
problems.code_hint: build(): top = 0 for q < 0.84; puffs only where d > 0.86

problems.detail: In the anime Angel Beach has puffy, lumpy Island Cloud ground, tall spiral-topped Skypiean palms, pastel white and cream houses with coloured rounded roofs and porches (Conis and Pagaya's house is a cosy two-tone house with a deck), the Waver beach and the Heaven's Gate and Upper Yard giant trees in the distance. Here the houses are grey domes, the palms are generic, and there is no colour palette beyond white, grey and blue.
Each cottage is one round sand-coloured floor with a few furniture blocks dropped in the middle. There are no partitions, wall shelves, rugs or porches; the interiors look empty from the cut.
problems.code_hint: I.furnish on a square inscribed in the circle (q = (r-1)/1.42), so the outer ring of each room stays bare

problems.where: under the island and around the sea ring
problems.detail: Puff spheres placed at y -10..-3 in the open air under the sea skin, and the finish pass removed 177 floating bits. The module scatters loose puffs that do not touch anything.
problems.code_hint: the 'cloud puffs drifting under and around' loop, the SEA_Y-2 puffs at 8%

problems.where: dark posts dotted across the plaza
problems.detail: The lamp posts and stall posts read as bare dark sticks on the white plate, with nothing round them.

top_fixes: Give every cottage its own silhouette: different sizes, a second smaller dome or tower, a cream/white quartz/calcite/cloud_bricks mix instead of white concrete, coloured roof caps (orange, pink, sky blue), a porch with steps and a railing, and round windows with frames. Make Conis's house a distinct two-storey house with a deck.
Sculpt the cloud ground: noise-driven mounds 1-4 high, puff clusters along the lanes, cloud dunes up to the beach, and a winding lane 2-3 wide edged with puffs, not a 1-block line on a flat plate.
Replace the generic palms with Skypiea's curled palms (a spiral crown, and coconut-like dial fruit) of mixed heights in clumps, and add flower beds with pastel colours.
Furnish the full round rooms: kitchen counters along the curved wall, a rug, shelves of dials, a loft, and hanging lamps from the dome.
Drop the free-floating puff spheres, or attach them to the island's underside as drips and stalactites of cloud, so nothing hangs in the air.

problems.where: all ~20 town houses in the four street blocks
problems.detail: Every house is a 9x9 or 8x9 box with four corner logs, flat infill, a row of single panes and the same orange gable roof, placed in a strict grid every 11 blocks. This is exactly the Nanohana problem: identical boxes in rows.
problems.code_hint: town_house(): fixed 9x9, walls() + 4 corner columns, windows every 2 blocks, no frame or jetty; lots loop with a fixed step of 11

problems.where: house walls and the tavern (north, CX±9)
problems.detail: There are no mid-wall posts, beams, sills, shutters or flower boxes worth the name. The tavern is a flat 19x15x11 stucco box with a fence rail on its flat roof.
problems.code_hint: town_house and the tavern block both use b.walls() with no frame

problems.detail: A perfectly square grid of grey cobble streets with flat green squares between. The round plaza is a flat disc, with nothing on it but a few lone posts and crates.

problems.where: flag behind the throne on the tavern roof
problems.detail: Buggy's flag is a 1-block-thick wool sheet, so from the back it reads mirrored and bare. The guide says flags must be 2 thick, with the design on both sides.
problems.code_hint: the 'Buggy's flag: skull with a red nose' loop sets one z layer only

problems.detail: In the anime Orange Town is a small, crooked harbour town of tall, narrow, half-timbered houses with orange tile roofs, balconies and shop signs, half wrecked by the Buggy Ball. Buggy holds court on the roof of the bar, which carries a huge striped circus tent on top. The town here is an orderly grid. There is no destruction (a crater is a hole in the street), and the Big Top sits in the square instead of on Buggy's building.
Rooms are small square boxes with a red rug and two blocks of furniture. All the houses read the same from above.
The cannon is a black block cross on a grey slab with three black spheres, crude and much darker than everything else.

top_fixes: Rewrite town_house to use townkit.house() with JETTY/frame styles: varied widths (6-11), 2-3 storeys, jettied upper floors, framed windows with shutters and flower boxes, balconies and shop signs. Vary roof colours (orange, terracotta, brown) and roof directions.
Break the grid: curve the streets and offset the lots with gaps, alleys and small yards. Raise or lower lots by 1-2 blocks with steps, and add market stalls, barrels and laundry lines between houses.
Make the Buggy Ball damage real: one row of houses smashed open with rubble piles, broken beams and scorch marks down the line of fire, not a round hole.

Give the tavern a framed facade, a bar sign board, balconies and a pitched or tiered roof under the throne terrace. Put the Big Top on or against the tavern as in the show, or at least tie it to Buggy's HQ.
Make the flag two blocks thick with the design on both sides, and rebuild the cannon with wheels and a carriage in wood and iron.

problems.detail: A plain stone-brick cylinder 22 high with three blue bands and pinhole windows. There is no buttress, no base flare, no balcony round the lantern room and no door frame. It reads as a grey can.

The giant relay Den Den Mushi, the whole point of the place, cannot be seen from outside. The glass is covered by the white floor ring and the dome, and the snail is a plain orange ellipsoid with no shell spiral, eyestalks or receiver. A Marine relay should show the snail's shell and stalks and the Marine gull/MARINE lettering, in blue and white Marine style.
problems.code_hint: b.shape(... orange_terracotta ...) ellipsoid inside the glass cylinder

problems.detail: Flat lawn everywhere with a few gravel lines. The 'sea' is a rectangular basin cut straight along the build edge, with a sand strip ruled along the south boundary, so it looks like a swimming pool, not a coast.
problems.code_hint: T.sea(... x > 50 + 2*sin(z*0.25)) inside a square NX x NZ

problems.detail: The tower's ground floor is empty bare stone. The radio room and lab floors have a handful of blocks; there are no banks of snail receivers, maps, desks or shelves.
The stone shed's roof renders as a black slab mass that dominates the north-west view.
The cross-arms are loose iron_bar stubs every 6 blocks, with no guy wires to the ground, so the mast looks unstable and fragmented.

top_fixes: Turn the tower into a proper Marine signal tower: a wider battered base with a door arch, string courses, framed windows, a railed balcony at the lantern level, and a glass lantern you can see into, with a large readable snail (spiral shell in two colours, eyestalks, a receiver cord).
Make the coast natural: a curved bay, rocky cliffs and boulders where the land meets the water, a shingle beach, and the jetty reaching out from rocks instead of a ruled rectangular pool.
Fill the radio room: walls of small den den mushi on shelves, desks with receivers, a map table, filing cabinets and lamps. Give the tower ground floor a guard room.
Add guy wires (chains or fences) from the mast to anchor blocks, and ground details: crates, a flagpole with the Marine flag (2 thick), lamp posts, a fenced garden and a few trees.
Swap the shed's black roof for Marine slate or blue tiles with an overhang and eaves.

problems.where: stone pteranodon on top of the keep (CX, y 39-50)
problems.detail: The pteranodon and its support column float 2 blocks above the keep roof: y 37-38 at (CX, PZ) is air. The roof tops out at y 36 and the column starts at KTOP+6 = 39. The finish pass logs 'big floating part kept=1'. The wings are thin one-block ribbons hovering over the keep.
problems.code_hint: for y in range(KTOP + 6, PY - 2): b.set(CX, y, PZ, chiseled...) — the pagoda_roof only rises to KTOP+3

problems.where: keep (KX0..KX1, 27 x 25 x 33) and curtain wall (61 x 61 x 14)
problems.detail: The keep is a flat black box with red slits every 4 blocks and a one-block slab skirt at each floor. The curtain wall runs 60 blocks without a buttress, set-back or tower between the corners. It is all one material (polished blackstone bricks).
problems.code_hint: b.walls(KX0,1,KZ0,KX1,KTOP,KZ1,BLACK); the curtain wall loop fills a 2-thick square

problems.detail: pagoda_roof over a 16x14 half-span with 3 layers comes out almost flat, a slate plate only 3 blocks high. It does not read as a flared Wano roof. The floor 'skirts' are flat rings, not eaves.

The courtyard is a flat checker of polished blackstone. The plain outside is a flat random speckle of basalt, blackstone and dirt, with single-block basalt sticks and 1x1 dead trees standing in a square grid area.

King's fortress is not a place shown in the anime. If it keeps the Kaido/Onigashima look it needs Wano castle grammar: stone ishigaki bases with sloped walls, white or black plaster with dark timber, stacked curved tile roofs with gables, and King's pteranodon and flame motifs. Right now it is a generic black box castle.
A huge empty courtyard. The barracks and forge are plain boxes; the keep's great hall is a big dark floor with a purple rug and little else.
The 'Kaido banners' are 6-block columns of purple and black wool stuck to the wall, with no pole or shape.

top_fixes: Connect the pteranodon to the roof: extend the column down to the ridge (or sit the beast on a raised plinth), and give it thicker, sculpted wings with finger bones and membrane, and a real head and beak.

Give the keep Wano castle grammar: a sloped stone ishigaki base, set-back storeys each with a deep flared curved roof (B.pagoda_roof per storey with a real overhang and rise), gables (chidori/kara-hafu), framed windows, and corner posts.

Break up the curtain wall: buttresses every 8-10 blocks, an intermediate tower on each side, a machicolated parapet, mixed materials (blackstone, basalt, deepslate tiles, a red-lacquer trim band) and braziers on corbels.
Shape the ground: a raised rocky mound under the fortress, cracked lava fissures with magma edges winding through, ash dunes, and clusters of basalt columns of varied height instead of single sticks.
Fill the courtyard with training grounds, a forge yard with chimneys and smoke, weapon racks and war-beast cages, and give the throne hall pillars, banners and a raised dais.

problems.detail: God Valley in the anime is a lush, heavily forested island (the natives were hunted through the jungle), with the Celestial Dragons' grand venue. This build has no trees at all: just flat lawn, a scorched disc, a white box and some huts.

A 50-long flat white concrete box with a flat solid-gold slab roof and two gold onion blobs on the corners. The colonnade is a row of plain quartz pillars. It has no pediment, no tiered roof, no dome, no stair towers and no ornament; the flat gold-block roof looks garish.

From outside the 'ruin' reads as a grey jagged rock mass. The side walls follow a sine height and the gable is a solid triangle, so you cannot tell it was a nave: no arches, no window tracery, no buttresses, no fallen vault ribs.
problems.code_hint: hh = int(12 + 6*sin(z*0.4)) for the side walls

problems.detail: Seven identical 9x8 shacks in a neat 2-column grid, burnt by randomly deleting planks, so they look like half-built boxes, not a village.
The tents are three black-wool lean-to bars that read as black slabs. The wreck is a dark flat-topped hull with no broken masts, no tilt and no ribs showing; it looks like a box sitting on the beach.
Flat lawn between features. The sea is a straight-edged rectangle along the south edge with a ruled sand strip, and the arena is a perfect disc.

problems.where: Garp's anchor ring and Rocks flag
problems.detail: The anchor is a column of iron blocks with a hollow ring floating on top (cyl at y 9). The flag on a fence pole is a flat 1-thick board.
Long empty white rooms with a few gold blocks and a rug. Nothing like a noble banquet hall: no chandeliers, no table runs, no tapestries.

top_fixes: Plant a real jungle: dense mixed big trees (2x2 trunks, layered canopies, vines, undergrowth) over half the island, with clearings for the village and the arena, so the island reads as God Valley.

Rebuild the palace as a grand Mary Geoise-style hall: a stepped podium, a central dome with a lantern, pediments over a colonnade, wings with pitched roofs, quartz/calcite/gold trim instead of a flat gold slab, and fountains and banners in front.
Make the cathedral a readable ruin: a nave outline with pointed arches, broken buttresses, a rose window frame, fallen rib segments and rubble piles, and moss and vines growing over it.

Make the native village organic: round or varied huts with thatch (hay/stairs) roofs on stilts, scattered on uneven ground among the trees, with paths, drying racks and the well as a centre. Burn them with charred posts and collapsed roofs, not random holes.
Turn the wreck into a broken ship: tilted hull, snapped masts lying on the sand, exposed ribs, torn sails. Make proper A-frame tents with poles, and attach the anchor ring to the shank.

problems.detail: Five plain stacked square boxes of stone bricks with a solid gold cube on top. It looks like a grey wedding cake, with no stairway, columns, carved faces, cornices or Joy Boy/Nika imagery. Ladders are the only way up.
problems.code_hint: for k in range(5): b.box(CX-hw, 1+k*4, ... ) ; b.box(CX-2,21,...,GOLD)

problems.detail: Four concentric rings of 6-high flat mossy walls. They look like a sewer ring or a target from above, not an ancient city.

A flat square grass plate, about 112x112. The 'jungle' is about 30 identical lollipop trees (a 1-wide log with a leaf ellipsoid) and the cove is a smooth half-oval pond. There is no hill, cliff or rocky shore, though the final island should be dramatic.

The anime shows very little of Laugh Tale, but what it shows is a striking rocky island approached by the Oro Jackson, with the crew's arrival, a laughing Roger, and a sense of awe. A flat field with a stone ziggurat and a pond is not 'the final island'. There is no monumental scale, no ancient giant ruins, and no dramatic coastline or sea stacks.
The gold ring is one block thick in a single plane, on two square pillars with a flat lintel. It reads as a flat gold ring from the side and has no sun rays or carving.
The ruins are random-height wall rectangles, with no columns, arches, doorways or toppled statues.
Three long narrow strip rooms. The treasure is 30 random gold blocks on the floor; the Poneglyph is a 1x2 block. Nothing grand about the room that holds the One Piece.

top_fixes: Give the island relief: a central rise or mountain with the temple on top, rocky cliffs and sea stacks round the cove, a beach with boulders, and terraced ancient platforms climbing up.

Rebuild the temple as a monumental stepped pyramid with a grand central staircase on each face, carved stone bands, pillared shrine on top, giant guardian statues, Joy Boy sun motifs and a gold-and-stone peak, not a gold cube.
Replace the target-ring labyrinth with an overgrown ancient city: broken colonnades, arches, fallen giant statue heads, stairways and plazas half swallowed by the jungle.
Make a real jungle: big 2x2 trees of varied species and heights, layered canopies, bushes, ferns, vines hanging off ruins and moss on stones.

Make the treasure vault worthy of the One Piece: piles of gold heaped up in mounds, a raised altar with the final Poneglyph (a big carved block), lit by braziers. Give the Sun Gate a thick (3-deep) ring with rays.

problems.detail: In the anime Tequila Wolf is a colossal bridge, many times taller than this, with tall multi-tier arches and a whole town on the deck, stretching to the horizon. Here it is a 104-block stone box on 6 squat piers, with the deck only 16 above the water.
A single flat stone-brick face with no cornice, string course, voussoirs round the arches, pier cutwaters or buttresses. The x=0 end is cut off flat as a sheer wall, so the bridge starts nowhere.
problems.code_hint: piers via b.box(px,-10,0,px+5,D-1,W-1); arch infill loop; nothing at x<0

problems.detail: The 'scaffolding' is a forest of separate yellow scaffold poles standing in the sea with no planks, ledgers or cross-bracing between them. They look like stray floating posts. The half-laid deck is randomly holed cobblestone.
problems.code_hint: for x in range(END, L): if x % 3 == 0: scaffolding columns at z 0, CZ, W-1

problems.detail: Identical shack boxes in a row every 14 blocks on a flat grey andesite road. Nothing like the anime's dense deck town.
The work boats are 1-layer plank rectangles lying flat on the water, with no hull shape, mast or oars.
The huts hold bunks and a few blocks. The soup kitchen and overseers' office read the same as the barracks.

top_fixes: Make it monumental: raise the deck to 35-45 with two tiers of arches (big lower arches, a smaller arcade above), pier cutwaters, a cornice and string courses, and voussoir rings in a contrasting stone.

Start and end the bridge properly: run it off both edges of the build, or fade the start into a ramp or abutment. Make the unfinished end a stepped broken edge with real scaffolding (ledgers, planks, braces, ladders, ropes and pulleys).

Build a deck town: 2-3 storey stone and timber houses packed along both sides of a central street, overseers' towers with roofs, chains and slave work gangs, stone block stacks and carts, lamps on posts.
Replace the flat plank boats with small hulled boats with masts and furled sails, moored with ropes to rings on the piers, and add stairs down the piers to landing stages.

problems.detail: A perfect ellipse of coarse dirt with rooted_dirt on (x*z)%5, which renders as a regular tiled grid. The rest of the island is a flat lawn of short grass and ferns. There are no rocks, craters from a hundred years of fighting, roots or water.
problems.code_hint: little_garden_camp.build: duel ground loop, coarse_dirt if (x*z)%5 else rooted_dirt

problems.detail: The volcano is a perfect stepped cone with ring stripes (stone and tuff every 3 layers), topped by a square lava crater ring and a campfire sitting on lava. It reads as a striped traffic cone, with no lava flows, ash slopes or irregularity.

70 identical lollipop trees: a straight 1-wide jungle_log trunk with a single ellipsoid of leaves. Little Garden is a prehistoric jungle of huge buttressed trees, giant ferns, cycads and palms. There are no understory layers, no giant trees and no dinosaurs.

Dorry's hut is a small stepped brown and grey wool cone (radius 10). Brogy's cave is a smooth hemisphere of stone. Neither has giant scale or character. In the show the giants are about 20 m tall and their camps hold giant skulls, huge bones, monster-sized meat on spits and their horned helmets.
problems.code_hint: Dorry: line poles + wool rings; Brogy: b.shape(... ellipsoid ...)

problems.detail: A white concrete stacked disc with a 1-wide wool candle. The Candle Service Set is a giant wax cake with a spinning candle, and the Candle House is missing entirely.

problems.where: inside the hut and the cave (cut3)
problems.detail: Inside: a slab of brown wool for the bed, a furnish() storage corner and a flat orange-wool rug. They are empty giant-scale rooms with no giant-scale props.

top_fixes: Make the jungle prehistoric: a few huge trees with 2x2 or 3x3 trunks, buttress roots and multi-layer canopies, plus cycads, palms, giant ferns, vines in curtains and fallen logs. Vary tree height and shape.
Rework the volcano with a noise-perturbed radius, ridges and gullies, a jagged crater rim, cooled black lava flows down one side, and ash or gravel slopes. No ring stripes.

Make the duel ground look battle-scarred: an irregular outline, craters, broken rocks, giant weapon gouges, scattered giant bones, and the dinosaur skeleton at real size (a T-rex skull, a big ribcage).

Give the giants their gear at giant scale: a horned helmet, a huge round shield, a giant skull seat, meat roasting on a spit over each bonfire, and the hut as a proper giant lean-to of tree trunks and hides.
Add Mr. 3's Candle House (a wax mansion) and a proper Candle Service Set cake with a wax 'spinning' candle and a wax platform.
Break the flat lawn with a stream, rocky outcrops and little hills.

problems.where: weather balls (12 round the main islet + 3 per small islet)
problems.detail: Each 'floating weather ball' is a 1.6-radius cube-ish blob of stained glass on a 4-9 high chain stuck in the ground. Rendered, they look exactly like lollipop trees (dark trunk, coloured canopy) standing on the islands rather than balloons drifting on tethers.
problems.code_hint: weather_ball(b,x,1,z,top,c): chain y0..top then sphere r1.6

problems.detail: In the show Weatheria's islets are linked by heavy chains, with the weather balls floating high. Here they are L-shaped boardwalks (straight along x, then a right-angle turn along z) that barely sag. They look like garden fences.

Every building is the same white-concrete cylinder with a blue band and a stepped white dome, just at different radii. The observatory tower is hidden behind the library dome. The palette is white concrete, which is flat.
The islets are flat discs of island_cloud with a ring of puffs. The tops are perfectly flat round plates, the kitchen garden is a 6x6 square of farmland, and nothing climbs or dips.
problems.code_hint: islet(): b.cyl(x,z,rr,y,y,CLOUD) with flat y=0 top

problems.detail: The finish pass reports 'propped up floating part=7, removed floating bit=9, removed floating lantern=1', which means the module places pieces in the air, most likely the bridge rail fences and lanterns off the islet edges.
problems.code_hint: rope bridge loop sets fences and lanterns at y+1..y+3 where the deck was skipped

problems.detail: The labs are birch floors with one small furnish() set in the middle. There are no weather instruments, barometers, globes, bookshelves lining the walls of the 'great library', or spiral stairs.

top_fixes: Float the weather balls for real: put them 10-25 blocks above the islets on long thin chain tethers anchored to a post with a winch, make them proper glass spheres (radius 2-3) with a light inside, and vary the heights so they read as balloons.
Link the islets with big hanging iron chains (catenary curves) plus one or two sagging rope bridges that run straight between islets, not L-shaped boardwalks.

Vary the architecture: Haredas' house, a tall observatory with a domed telescope room above every other roof, the library as a big round hall with a gallery, and different dome shapes and colours (sky-blue tiles, quartz, glass). Use calcite or quartz instead of white concrete.
Sculpt the cloud islets with bumpy, multi-level cloud tops, puffs climbing the building bases, wisps hanging below, and a cloud-sea pond.
Furnish the library with full bookshelf walls, ladders, lecterns and a mezzanine ring, and the lab with weather devices (lightning rods, copper, glass orbs) and charts.

problems.where: hall shell, all four sides (x 14-66, z 18-62)
problems.detail: A 52x44 box of near-black red nether bricks, 16 high, with blackstone posts every 6 and a few tiny red panes. No set-backs, arches, cornice relief or real windows; from the NW it is a dark slab.
A flat black plate with a hemispherical terracotta dome dropped in the middle and gold blocks dotted on the parapet. The dome has no drum, windows or lantern.

The tiered seats are a solid brown ramp of dark_oak_planks filling the whole width, which reads as a big brown slab. The Celestial Dragons' box is a flat plank shelf on the east wall reached by a ladder. The stage is a plank box in front of a flat red wool sheet. There is no fan-shaped seating, no aisles, and no hanging lights apart from lanterns.

problems.detail: In the anime the Human Auctioning House is a theatre in Grove 1 among the mangrove roots, with a curved front and its big HUMAN AUCTIONING HOUSE sign, and a curved, semicircular auditorium facing a curtained stage. Here the facade is a quartz portico on a black box, the sign only says AUCTION, and the mangrove roots don't touch the building.
A flat lawn with tufts. The two Yarukiman trees stand far from the building, and the guard post is a lone teal shed.

top_fixes: Give the shell depth: pilasters with arches between them, tall arched windows, a cornice, and set-backs or curved corners; lighten the palette (red with sandstone or quartz trim instead of near-black)
Put the dome on a drum with windows and a lantern, and give the flat roof a slope or balustrade
Rebuild the auditorium as curved, stepped rows of seats with aisles, chandeliers, and a raised VIP box at the back
Make the bubbles sit on roots or the ground (as in shakky_bar.bubble) so they survive the finish pass
Bring a Yarukiman's roots up against the building, and write HUMAN AUCTIONING HOUSE on a curved sign board

problems.detail: Each 'cactus rock' is a straight cylinder in horizontal bands of terracotta and green terracotta every 3 blocks, so it looks like a striped barrel or totem, not a cactus. The arms are boxy horizontal cylinders. The anime's cactus mountains are huge saguaro shapes with vertical ribs and crowds of grave crosses on top.
A flat red-sand plate with a perfect cross of sandstone streets. The town sits in a valley among the rocks in the anime; here there is no slope, no terrace and no plaza shape.
Boxes of the same size (8-10 x 7-9) from T.house on a grid of spots, in sand, brick or plaster. There are no welcome banners across the facades, few signs, and no balconies.
The party hall is a 31x19 box of cut red sandstone with posts every 4 and single orange panes. Its gable end is a big blank orange wall (clearly visible in the SE render).
The gravestones are single stone_brick_walls scattered on the rock bands; at this scale they read as noise, not crosses.

top_fixes: Rebuild the cactus rocks as saguaro mountains: a ribbed, all-green trunk (vertical ridges, not stripes), rounded arms that bend upward, and a darker rocky base
Cover the rock tops with grave crosses (fence plus a trapdoor or wall arm) so they read
Lay the town in a valley with stepped terraces and an open plaza in front of the party hall
Make the houses varied: 2-3 storey Western/European fronts with balconies, signs, WELCOME banners and lantern strings
Give the party hall a decorated gable (a sign, a big round window, timbering) and a grand entrance with an awning

problems.detail: The tents are stepped wool A-frames that look like little red, black or white pyramids of blocks, with white stripes every 5. The canvas has no sag, no guy ropes and no pegs, and the wall loop leaves the gable ends solid wool on both ends.

A hull with a single mast and a square_sail. The sail does billow (belly=1), but the ship is not tilted or run up on the sand: it floats level in the water. It has no rigging, the deck is empty, and there is no gangplank to the beach.
A flat lawn behind a flat beach strip. The camp items are tiny: a 5-block campfire ring, a 5-wide plank wanted board and three crates.
Each tent has a one-call furnish() in a 2-3 high space.
The palms are a log with a one-block kink and a flat ellipsoid leaf blob, all in an evenly spaced row along the back edge.

top_fixes: Make the tents read as canvas: a sagging ridge, flared sides of slabs and stairs, guy ropes (fences or chains) to pegs, open flaps
Tilt the caravel on the sand with its bow up the beach; add shrouds, a gangplank, crates on deck and a patched sail
Add life to the camp: drying racks, a cook spit over the fire, hammocks between palms, a lookout ladder, a treasure pile
Curve the palms (leaning trunks with frond-shaped leaves) and scatter them unevenly
Give the beach dunes and rocks, and a path that winds from the fire to the ship

problems.detail: The keep is a 40x18x20 white concrete slab with a flat blue roof and a single-thick white billboard on top carrying MARINE. Windows are panes every 3 blocks. It has no tower, frame or set-back.

The curtain wall is 9-high flat white concrete with one blue stripe. The corner towers are plain 7x7 square concrete boxes with blue caps. Concrete everywhere reads flat; the guide says concrete is accent only.
The drill yard is a perfect smooth_stone/andesite checkerboard ((x+z)%2) over the whole 80x58 interior, with training posts in a straight grid. Outside is flat lawn.

The Shells Town 153rd branch is a tall white tower with MARINE painted vertically and the big gull emblem, crowned by Captain Morgan's statue, inside a high white wall where Zoro was tied to the post. This build is a low flat office block with a roof sign: no statue, no vertical tower, no Zoro execution post.
The flag is a flat single-thick wool rectangle on iron bars, one-sided, with no Marine gull.

top_fixes: Make the centrepiece a tall stepped white tower, marine_bricks or white terracotta with quartz trim, with MARINE written vertically on its face and the gull emblem, topped by a Morgan statue with his axe-hand.
Break up the keep with pilasters, balconies, window frames, a pitched blue-tile roof with overhang, and a columned entrance with an awning.
Replace the concrete curtain wall with marine_bricks and quartz trim, buttresses and a wall walk with parapet; make the towers round with conical blue roofs.
Pave the yard with varied stone and a parade path, add Zoro's post in a fenced patch, and plant some flower beds.
Make the flag double-sided with a Marine gull.

problems.detail: The castle is a 36x28x14 pink concrete box with a dead-flat magenta concrete roof and 4 plain cylinder towers in the corners. There are no gables, roofs, set-backs, balconies or windows beyond a few panes. The front heart is a single-thick red disc.

The island is flat lawn with 25% random decorations. Peonies and alliums render as dark grey-green specks everywhere, so the meadow looks littered with stones. There are no hills, beaches, gardens or curving paths.
These are stock plaster townkit houses recoloured by global string replace (white->pink, red nether->cherry). They are identical boxes with no Okama flair.
problems.code_hint: for k,v in b.blocks.items(): replace white_concrete -> PINK

problems.detail: The ballroom is a big quartz floor with a magenta pattern rug and almost nothing else: no columns, stage, chandeliers or mirrors.

Momoiro Island in the Kamabakka Kingdom is a lurid pink, heart-themed island: a frilly pink castle with heart arches, odd pink palm trees, heart topiary and okama glitter. Here only four towers with heart tops say 'Kamabakka'; the giant flowers are small 1-block-petal stars.
Small 1-2 column grass and dirt islands are left detached below and outside the outline.

top_fixes: Rebuild the castle with layered pink wings, steep magenta roofs (not a flat plate), heart-shaped arched windows and doorways, balconies, frilly white trim and conical tower roofs.
Shape the island: rolling hills, a pink sand beach, curved paths, and heart topiary and flower beds in groups instead of a 25% decoration carpet. Drop the peony spam.
Give the cottages custom Okama styling: round windows, striped awnings, heart signs, frilly cornices, varied shapes.
Make the giant flowers bigger, with layered petals of 2-3 rings and a thick stem with leaves.
Furnish the ballroom with columns, chandeliers, a stage, mirrors and a pink checkered floor.

problems.detail: The lab is a 52x32x22 white concrete box with cyan floor bands and a flat grey roof plate with a white dome on top. Every face is the same window grid. There are no wings, connecting tubes, vents, catwalks or entrance canopy.

The fire half is dead-flat noisy blackstone/basalt/magma confetti with 3 sine lava lines. The ice half is a flat snow plate with a frozen-lake oval. There are no volcano, ridges, craters, ice cliffs or snow drifts, and the split between the halves is a straight sine line.
problems.code_hint: rnd.choice of 4 top blocks per cell; cold = x+4sin < MIDX

problems.detail: The tank pipes are b.line diagonals of single iron blocks, connected only at corners. 80 'floating bits' were removed, so the pipes and parts of the letters are broken. The R-66 text reads as teal smudges.
problems.code_hint: b.line((tx,8,tz),(X0..,12,tz), iron_block); finish removed floating bit=80

problems.detail: The ground floor is mostly empty grey floor behind glass partitions, with crates stacked in two corners and one amethyst tank. The labs are generic subdivide rooms.

In the show Punk Hazard has a burning half with a volcano and a frozen half with snowy mountains and the lake. Caesar's lab is a big complex half-buried by the elements, with the gas-producing vents and the frozen tanker. The wrecked 'tanks' here are two grey boxes, and the Smiley and SAD vats are a tiny cylinder.

top_fixes: Give the terrain real relief: a volcano with a crater and lava falls on the hot side, snowy ridges, ice cliffs and drifts on the cold side, and a crack or rift line between them.

Break the lab into wings at different heights, linked by glass tube corridors, with exterior pipes (solid runs along walls), vents with smoke, catwalks and a big entrance canopy. Replace the flat roof with mechanical penthouses.
Replace the diagonal b.line pipes with face-connected pipe runs (elbows), and write R-66 on a sign board.
Build the SAD vat chamber as a big tank room with stairs and walkways; fill the ground floor with lab benches, specimen tanks and consoles.
Add a frozen tanker hulk in the lake and wrecked vehicles half-buried in snow.

problems.detail: There is a forest of iron chains: the module lights nothing, so finish.lighting added 342 lights. In this 30-high cavern each is a lantern hung on a chain 20-26 blocks long from the roof, filling cut8/cut16 with hundreds of black vertical lines.
problems.code_hint: finish.place_light(): 'if h >= 6: ... for k in range(ly+1, y+h): iron_chain' (no cap on chain length); module has no own lighting

problems.detail: The dead-tree branches step diagonally: each segment is offset by j//2 in y, so branch blocks touch only by an edge. 77 floating bits were removed and the trees end up half-limbed.
