problems.detail: The w7_house() variants are better than most (multi-storey, coloured roofs, chimneys), but they are all the same rectangular gable box. No balconies, no arcades at canal level, no stilts or bridges between buildings, no towers.

problems.where: Galley-La HQ south-west of the dock (around 800,740 in the SE view)
problems.detail: A huge dark-brown flat board stands behind the hip roof: the back of the 'GALLEY' sign, a plain single-colour slab with no frame or text on that side. The HQ is a flat-sided 3-storey box with a pyramid roof.
The ships under construction are a muddled brown mass of planks in the slips, with no readable hull shape, ribs or scaffolding pattern. Yellow fence posts stand loose round them.

The Great Fountain should be a huge water spout over a tiered stone basin at the top of the city. The blue-and-white block cone reads as a solid blue pillar and not as falling water. Dock 1 in the anime has giant hammerhead cranes and a massive gate with a big '1' sign. These red gantries are thin and plain. There are no Yagara bull boats in the canals.
CUTS = [] so no interior is rendered, and the houses and HQ cannot be checked inside.

top_fixes: Pack the houses densely along the canals with shared walls, ground-floor arcades over the water, balconies, flower boxes, and bridges and walkways linking buildings. Fill the outer ring instead of leaving bare paving.
Rebuild the HQ as Iceburg's mansion: set-backs, a central tower, a columned entrance and a proper two-sided framed sign.
Give Dock 1 a huge gate with the '1', big hammerhead cranes with booms and hanging hooks on chains, ships in the slips with clear hull shapes and ribs, and scaffolding.
Make the fountain read as water: a white foam crown and translucent blue glass and water sheets falling into stepped basins, with a visible pedestal.
Add CUTS so interiors are checked, and add boats and Yagara bulls on the canals, mooring posts, lamps and cafe terraces.

problems.detail: The castle stands on a perfectly round, perfectly flat crag plateau. It is solid deepslate and tuff up to y6 out to radius 30, then a linear ramp down; cut4 shows it as a huge flat grey disc. A crag should be rough, rocky and stepped. This raised solid plinth is also what makes the build stand up above the terrain it is placed on.

The main block is a 41x27 box of deepslate bricks with one material everywhere. Thin red slit windows are on a 4-block grid and buttresses every 8. The long walls have no setbacks, no tracery, no rose window, and no material change between floors, so the whole thing reads as one dark monolith.

The anime castle is a sprawling, partly ruined gothic mass with crooked spires, broken walls and a gloomy multi-wing silhouette above a misty forest and the ruined Shikkearu town. Here it is a tidy rectangle with symmetrical round towers. The curled Tim Burton hills are a nice touch, but the dead trees are pale-oak poles with 3-block right-angle branches that look like crosses.
Small pink blocks are scattered loose on the courtyard in front of the gate (Perona décor?), and they read as debris. The finish pass removed floating carpets, so some rooms lost rugs.

top_fixes: Make the crag natural: rough cliff faces of tuff and deepslate with outcrops, ledges and a winding path, instead of a flat-topped disc. Let the castle footprint step down the rock.

Break the monolith: add a different trim material (polished blackstone or stone for string courses), pointed-arch windows with tracery and a rose window on the gable, wings at different heights, a few collapsed sections, and crooked or uneven spire heights.
Replace the cross-shaped trees with twisted dead trees that branch at angles, with hanging pale moss and mist (cobweb/ash) patches.
Add the ruined Shikkearu town as streets of broken houses with partial roofs, plus the Humandrill camp and Zoro's training ground with broken weapons.

problems.detail: Only 5 Yarukiman mangroves stand in the corners, and they are short (h 22-28) next to a Ferris wheel 49 high. On Sabaody the mangroves are colossal, with big painted grove numbers on their trunks, and they tower over everything. The bubbles are pale-blue cube clusters on the lawn instead of round, translucent bubbles rising from the roots.
The ticket hall, café, staff house and prize shop are the standard red-roofed T.house 'plaster' boxes and do not match the pink and white fairground style.
The SABAODY / PARK lettering on the gate reads as a red blob from both angles. The Ferris wheel spokes are iron bars that look like grey clutter.
problems.where: gate z~90; Ferris wheel x27 z36

problems.detail: Between the attractions the ground is a flat lawn of scattered flowers. There are no mangrove roots running across the park, no grove dips and no raised paths.

top_fixes: Make the mangroves huge (radius 6-8, height 50+), with arching root systems and grove numbers painted on the trunks with b.text. Let them define the park's edge and canopy.
Build bubbles as round hollow spheres of translucent bubble block at several sizes, rising from the roots at different heights. Group them along the roots instead of as cubes on the grass.
Restyle the park buildings in candy-stripe fairground style: domed or pointed tent roofs, pink and white walls, scalloped awnings, signs.
Make the gate lettering readable: a darker board, letters with spacing and an outline, and thicker letters or a simpler font. Use white concrete or chain spokes on the wheel.
Add ground interest: root arches over paths, raised walkway platforms, flower beds with borders, and stalls along the boulevard.

problems.detail: The sails billow (square_sail with belly), which is good, but the emblem on the sails is a generic black skull and crossbones. Whitebeard's mark is a skull with a white crescent moustache in front of a cross. The masthead flag shows the same generic skull.

A vast, flat, empty birch deck with rows of barrels and a couple of masts. The cut at y 12 shows a featureless plank sheet. There are no hatches, gratings, capstans, ship's boats on deck, cannon rows or deck houses.
Three stacked boxy tiers with flat sand-coloured roofs and windows ruled in rows. It has no galleries, no carved stern windows, no lanterns and no lettering, so it reads like an office block.
CUTS = [12, 18]: y 12 is the deck itself, so neither cut shows the gun deck (GUN_Y 5) or the hold (y -2). You cannot check those interiors from the renders.
The head reads, but its top is a flat grey hollow plate. The real Moby Dick's whale head has a big friendly grin with a defined lip line, round eyes with a ridge, and a smooth rounded crown.
The wheels are a thin single-plane ring of red terracotta with a thin arch for a housing. They need a solid paddle box.

top_fixes: Fix the emblem: the Whitebeard Jolly Roger (skull with a white crescent moustache over a cross) on the main sails and the flag, 2 thick so it reads from both sides.

Dress the deck: hatches with gratings, capstans, rows of cannons at the rails, ship's boats on chocks, mast fife rails, rope coils and a central deckhouse, so the 40-wide deck is not a flat plank field.
Rebuild the stern castle with stepped galleries and balustrades, framed stern windows, lanterns at the corners, carved trim and a curved transom. Give Whitebeard's giant chair a canopy.
Set CUTS to show the gun deck and the hold (e.g. [8, -1, 18]), and check that those rooms are furnished and lit.
Round off the whale head crown, define the grin and eyes, and give the paddle wheels solid side housings.

problems.detail: The hill is int(6 - d/4) concentric 1-block rings. It reads as contour lines or a wedding-cake mound, not a natural slope.
The tangerine trees sit in a regular 6x4 grid, (i%6)*5 by (i//6)*6, all the same shape, like an orchard plotted on graph paper. Bellemere's grove in the show is dense and irregular round her house.
Twelve stock townkit houses are dropped on a fixed spot list. They are all the same height and plan, with no porches, fences, gardens, washing lines or boats.
The square is a perfect 18x16 stone-brick rectangle with a well. Most of the village ground is flat lawn with 5% random flowers.

problems.detail: Bellemere's house is a generic 'orange' townkit box. In the show it is a small white cottage with a red roof on the slope, fenced in by the grove. Also missing: Genzo's house with the pinwheel, Nako's clinic sign, and the tall Arlong-era mill and wall.
The fishing pier is a tiny stub with no boats, nets or fish racks.

top_fixes: Replace the ring hill with a smooth noise slope that has terraced, irregular grove rows following the contours, and let the trees vary in height.
Make Bellemere's house a bespoke white cottage with a red roof, porch, garden table, laundry line and mikan crates, framed by the grove and a wooden fence.
Give the village houses porches, fences, gardens and different heights and roof colours, set along a curving lane instead of fixed spots.
Turn the square into an irregular plaza with cobble variation, benches and a big pinwheel at Genzo's house; extend the pier with fishing boats and nets.

problems.detail: The Marine base compound wall is a flat run of white concrete with a blue cap and fence spikes. The HQ building is a tall box whose front is flat white with thin pilaster strips. MARINE is painted on it, but there is no cornice, window depth or entrance portico.
A small dirt chunk floats off the south-east plate edge, separate from the ground, in every view. It comes from the rim or skirt.
problems.where: SE view about (880,700); cut views about (880,520)
problems.code_hint: pipeline.soften_edges skirt, or the module's ground edge

problems.detail: The town sits on a flat lawn with straight grey paths. There are no fences, gardens, market square, steps or slope down to the canal.

The Morgan statue is a grey block figure with a flat white slab for its axe-hand. The show's Shells Town has a tall Marine HQ with the huge Morgan statue on top (which Luffy pulls down), the yard where Zoro was tied to a post, and Rika's family restaurant in a brick and orange-roof town. The town here is generic timber houses, all dark red or brown roofs of the same size.
The town houses repeat with the same footprint and roof pitch and are laid out in rows. Several roofs read as flat dark slabs from above.

top_fixes: Give the HQ depth: a stepped top with a cornice, deep window reveals, an entrance portico with columns and the Marine gull over it, and a flagpole with a two-sided Marine flag.
Sculpt Morgan properly: a coat with epaulettes, a jaw, and a clear axe-hand (an iron/grey blade shape), standing on a plinth.
Break the compound wall with gate towers, buttresses and lamps, and put the 'Zoro post' yard inside with a training ground.

Vary the town: different house sizes and roof colours (orange and terracotta), a market square with a well and stalls, Rika's restaurant sign, gardens with fences, and a sloping street down to the canal quay.
Remove the floating dirt chunk on the SE rim (check soften_edges for islands cut off from the skirt).

problems.where: both masts, the yellow/white swags under each yard (z = CZ+1)

problems.detail: In the show the yards are tilted up in a V, the masts are tall and thin, and the BT flags are small swallow-tail pennants. Here the yards are flat horizontal, and each flag is an 11x7 slab of red wool that looks bigger than a sail. The top floor in the show has a front gable carrying RESTAURANT and a red door. Here RESTAURANT is mostly hidden under the hip roof's overhang. The fish head should be a carp head with thick yellow-orange lips and a flat-ish face. Here it is a rounded white dome with a black eye blob.

Cut 22 shows the storage room as a random heap of crates and barrels with no shelving or layout. The dining hall is a grid of identical white-dot tables with no centrepiece, no stage, no chandeliers visible and no captain's table. The fish-head interior is a black void.

The tiers are straight-sided boxes with flat walls between the windows. There are no pilasters, the balcony rails don't stand out from the wall, and the hull side has no curve or tumblehome above the deck.

top_fixes: Draw the swags with depth: offset each scallop 1-3 blocks forward (+/-z) by sin(), or call canvas.square_sail with a stripe pattern, and tilt the yards upward like the reference
Replace the fence-stair shrouds with proper rope ladders (chains/ladder blocks on a straight line, from the deck rail to the mast top) that touch at both ends
Shrink the BT flags to small 2-thick pennants with a swallow-tail cut, and raise the masts
Give the top floor a front gable with RESTAURANT on it and a red door, as in the reference; move the text out from under the eave
Reshape the fish head: flatter face, big yellow/orange lips round the open mouth, round eyes set at the sides
Furnish the storage/attic floor properly (shelves, sacks on racks) and add chandeliers and a centre feature to the dining hall

problems.detail: The ground is a perfectly flat lawn disk at y=0 with a straight cross of avenues. There are no rises, ravines, roots, ferns, undergrowth or water. Upper Yard should be a dense jungle.
problems.code_hint: b.set(x,0,z, grass/moss) flat; avenues along CX/CZ lines

problems.detail: The ruins are near-identical rectangular stumps with sine-broken tops on an even ring (r 28-44). Their tops read as noise, with no collapsed arches, carved friezes, stepped bases or fallen blocks.
117 floating bits were removed: the branch logs step diagonally (by + i//3), so they break apart, and vines are placed without support.
The island clouds are flat white plates with straight undersides that look like dinner plates under the ruins, rather than lumpy cumulus.
There are only a few furnished spaces. The temple and ruins are mostly empty shells, which suits ruins but has little to discover: no altar room or Poneglyph chamber detail.

top_fixes: Add gentle hills, roots, ferns and bushes over the ground, mossy stone patches, a stream or pool, and broken paving instead of straight avenues.
Give the ruins carved character: stepped bases, gold spiral friezes, collapsed arches and fallen columns, and vary their footprints and spacing.
Make tree branches face-connected (step x/z then y) so they survive the floating pass, and hang vines from leaves or logs.
Give the cloud shelves puffy, lumpy undersides with varied thickness.
Add a Poneglyph chamber in the temple with torches and offerings.

problems.detail: Big Mom's throne room is a huge empty white disk about 45 blocks across, with a red carpet line, a yellow gold-block slab for a throne, and r.scatter dropping random cakes, candles and blocks around like litter. There are no columns, wall decor, dais steps, banners or chandeliers.
The finish pass hung 96 long chains with lanterns from the very high ceilings. The hall is a forest of dark vertical bars that looks like a cage.

problems.detail: There are 34 cake_house boxes with stepped concrete ring roofs in one even ring at radius 64-74. Only the colours vary; every shape is the same, and they look like rows of pyramids.
problems.code_hint: cake_house(): b.walls + concentric concrete rings roof

problems.detail: The plaza is a huge flat pink-and-white checker annulus. The city ground is flat lawn with decorations, and there are no canals, bridges, hills or the Seducing Woods' density.
The tiers are perfect cylinders. The drip frosting helps, but the walls between turrets are smooth, with few windows, balconies or doors on the upper tiers.

top_fixes: Furnish the throne room: a stepped dais with a huge candy throne, columns with frosting capitals, banners, chandeliers on short chains, and tables laid with cakes instead of scattered litter.
Cap ceiling height or add mezzanine floors so the lighting uses chandeliers rather than 20-block chains.
Make Sweet City houses actual cake and candy shapes: round layer-cake houses, cupcake domes, gingerbread gables. Vary them, and lay them along curved streets.
Break the plaza with candy-cane fountains, flower and lollipop beds, and a chocolate river or canal with biscuit bridges; make the Seducing Woods dense and spooky.
Add arched windows, balconies and doors on every tier, plus spiral stairs or bridges between turrets.

problems.detail: The outer drum's arches read as tall rectangular slots in a uniform wall: the openings are recessed only one block and there are no round arch heads, keystones, engaged columns or balustrades. From a distance it is a tan cylinder with vertical stripes.

problems.detail: The royal box canopy is a red/yellow checkerboard, which the building guide explicitly forbids. It also sits as a flat slab on posts with no scalloped edge or drape.
problems.where: north side canopy (NW view, left of arena)

problems.detail: The three tiers of seating are one monotone sandstone slope of slabs. There are no bench rows in a contrasting material, no railings at the podium edges, no crowd colour (red/orange/yellow wool cushions) and no stair handrails.

The crown of the drum is a flat sandstone ring (see cut12): no parapet wall, no masts for an awning, nothing on the skyline. The flags are a single wool block plus one beside it on a fence: tiny lollipops, not banners.
problems.where: y H+1 ring; flag poles every 15 degrees

problems.detail: The under-stand rooms are bare spruce floors between grey stone-brick radial walls with a few furnish pieces. They are dark wedge-shaped cells with no ceiling beams, wall lamps, weapon racks along the curved walls or the toy-prisoner cages the show has. The 184 auto-added lights mean the module itself lights almost nothing.

The show's Corrida Colosseum is a tall, festive drum with orange-red upper storeys, many coloured banners, a big grand stairway and entrance, and the arena ring with fighting fish in the moat. The stage here is a flat grey disk, the moat is plain water with no fins, and there is no grand stair entrance or Dressrosa flower decoration outside.

top_fixes: Carve real arches into the outer facade: 2-3 block deep recesses with round heads (stairs/slabs), keystones, engaged pilasters with caps between bays and a balustrade at each storey. Make the upper storey orange terracotta with a heavy cornice.
Replace the checkerboard canopy with striped red/gold awning cloth that sags (curved, with a scalloped edge), plus a proper royal balcony with a railing and banners.
Detail the stands: alternate bench rows (spruce/stairs) with sandstone risers, add coloured cushions, podium railings, and handrails on the radial stairs.
Crown the drum with a parapet, tall masts with long two-sided red/yellow banners (3-5 blocks, waving) and statues over the four gates.
Light and dress the under-stand rooms: ceiling beams, wall lamps, weapon racks, cages for the toy prisoners, and a vaulted gate tunnel with torches.
Give the stage a textured surface (cracked stone, blood-red patches, a ring of posts) and add fins and lily-pad debris in the moat; add a grand stairway and fountains to the main entrance outside.
